page_numbering.basis: ChromaDB metadata page_number (0-based) — this is what retrieval_trace will carry
page_numbering.doc_slug: cases default to doc_slug 'manual' (RT-SVD03L-EN) unless they specify expected_doc_slug

corpus_docs.manual: RT-SVD03L-EN ReliaTel Controls Service & Diagnostic (176 pp) — fault codes, LED, terminal voltages, sequences
corpus_docs.rt-svx075a-en-12022022: RT-SVX075A-EN IOM (68 pp) — install, startup, MAINTENANCE, refrigerant charging
corpus_docs.rt-prc107b-en-07152023: RT-PRC107B-EN Product Catalog (108 pp) — electrical data (MCA/fuse), capacities (MBh/EER/IEER), 6-25T high-efficiency models
corpus_docs.rt-svu03l-en-01132017: RT-SVU03L-EN Owner manual (2-pp stub, low value)

grading.retrieval_recall: fraction of a case's expected_pages present in retrieval_trace; aggregate target >= 0.80, per-case override via recall_min. recall_mode 'any' (fault cases) scores 1.0 if ANY expected page is hit — ground truth there is a troubleshooting-table REGION, not a single page
grading.routing: expected_route must match the agent's actual output mode (job_card | artifact | text | clarify | refuse); a LIST means any listed route is acceptable (genuinely ambiguous intent). expect_payload_any replaces expect_job_card/expected_artifact on those cases
grading.structural: expected_artifact type, expect_job_card, expect_image, must_contain, must_not_contain, must_cite_page
grading.faithfulness: cases with faithfulness=true get one binary LLM-judge call: is every factual claim supported by retrieval_trace? aggregate pass-rate target >= 0.90

cases.query: The RTRM system green LED is blinking twice every two seconds. What does this mean and how do I find the specific fault?
cases.persona_note: Tech on the roof reading the board's LED before opening anything.
cases.reference_notes: FAITHFULNESS TRAP. p.33 (page_number 32) 'RTRM System LED Diagnostic Indicator' states 2x quarter-second blinks every 2s = ONE OR MORE of ~20 diagnostics (supply fan fail, gas heat fail, OAT sensor fail, frostat, smoke detector, RTOM comm fail, etc.). p.77 (76) repeats it and points back to p.33. A correct answer must NOT name a single root cause — it must say a diagnostic is present and direct the tech to enter TEST mode to identify which. Judge should fail any answer that asserts a specific fault. CALIBRATED 2026-06-09 (run #1): agent routed to artifact, which is CORRECT per its own system-prompt rule 'LED code / flash code -> render_artifact'; products.json fault_examples simultaneously says '2-flash -> job card'. Both readings are defensible (symptom phrasing vs code lookup), so expected_route accepts either and expect_payload_any requires that one of the two payloads exists. Recall was 1.0 (32+76 both retrieved).

cases.query: The unit isn't cooling. The compressor won't start and there are no fault diagnostics showing on the RTRM. How do I diagnose this?
cases.persona_note: No-cool service call, board shows nothing — the hardest field case.
cases.reference_notes: p.36 (page_number 35) has the exact list 'Compressor Will not Run, no Diagnostics': frostat trip, compressor disable input open, unit economizing/OA damper not yet 100%, unit in heat/off mode, Tracer/BMS demand limit. Web (support.trane.com) adds field steps: jump R->Y1 on RTRM, check LPC/HPC open, 20-26 VAC at contactor coil, 3-phase voltage, locked rotor. Steps should map to these; each step needs a citation. CALIBRATED 2026-06-09 (run #1): the no-run troubleshooting table is a REGION spanning printed pp.35-38 (page_number 34-36); run #1 retrieved 36 (printed 37, the SERVICE/LPC continuation) and scored 0.00 under single-page truth — widened to the region with recall_mode any.

cases.query: The rooftop unit shuts down about 40 seconds after startup and the SERVICE LED is pulsing. I think the fan proving switch isn't operating right.
cases.persona_note: Classic 40-second trip — proving/fan-fail switch.
cases.reference_notes: VERIFIED in PDF. p.34 (page_number 33): Service LED PULSING = fan proving switch [fan fail switch FFS] failed to open (3-25T) / close (27.5-50T) before 40 seconds; unit runs 40s then stops. p.37 (36) restates it under SERVICE: 'supply fan proving switch (FFS) has failed to open within 40 seconds after the fan starts or has closed during fan operation' — this is the better page since it ties to a measurement. p.33 (32) lists 'Supply fan fail' among the 2-flash diagnostics. Note tonnage dependency (open 3-25T vs close 27.5-50T) — answer must not assert the wrong direction.

cases.query: No heat — I'm getting a heat fail diagnostic on the RTRM. The gas valve isn't opening. What should I check?
cases.persona_note: Gas heat no-light call.
cases.reference_notes: CALIBRATED 2026-06-09 (run #1): retrieved 34/35/118/121 — the ignition-sequence region spans printed pp.119-120 (page_number 118-119), so 118 added and recall_mode any (region truth). RESOLVED by domain review of the PDF. p.36 (35): 'E1 flashing indicates a Heat Failure diagnostic'. p.120 (119): ignition control (IGN) self-check sequence — verifies gas valve de-energized, checks high limit (TCO1/TCO2) closed, pressure switch (PS) open, flame rollout (FR) closed; 20s pre-purge; spark 2-7s. Confirmed this manual has NO 'IGN module flashes N times = X' code table (p.78 LED tables cover comms/LCI LEDs only, not an ignition blink code), so I removed the original 'ignition LED flashing 2 times' phrasing — it would have invited a hallucinated code lookup. Correct answer checks TCO1/PS/FR/gas valve/spark per the p.120 sequence + the RTRM E1 flag.

cases.query: The compressor keeps short cycling — runs 3-4 minutes then trips, and the cool fail indicator is pulsing. How do I check the high and low pressure cutout circuits?
cases.persona_note: Short-cycling on a pressure cutout.
cases.reference_notes: RESOLVED by domain review. The exact short-cycle-on-pressure logic is p.37 (page_number 36): 'LPC 1 or LPC 2 has opened during the 3 minute minimum on time during 4 consecutive compressor starts' -> cooling lockout, with test points 'measure RTRM J1-8 (LPC1) / J3-2 (LPC2) to chassis ground, 24 VAC should be present at all times'. p.158 (157) covers the LPC lockout incremental counter and compressor-disable behavior. (My earlier guess p.148 was wrong — that page is humidity setpoint.) The phrase 'short cycling' is sparse in the corpus (2 hits) so retrieval leans on 'low pressure'/'LPC'/'lockout'; weak recall here would be a genuine retrieval finding.

cases.query: I'm getting an economizer fault. The mixed air temperature reading looks wrong and I think the damper position is off. How do I diagnose the economizer module?
cases.persona_note: Economizer not modulating / bad MAT.
cases.reference_notes: p.55 (54), Figure 48: economizer setup + fault states COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE / MAT SENSOR FAULT / OAT SENSOR. p.126 (125): economizer module has a diagnostic LED (ON = OK to economize). Confirm these are the diagnose pages vs. the wiring figures (16/17).

cases.query: The clogged filter indication keeps coming on. What does it actually mean and what should I check?
cases.persona_note: Maintenance / nuisance-alarm call.
cases.reference_notes: RESOLVED by domain review. p.34 (33): Service reading ON = clogged filter switch closed >= 2 minutes => clogged filter. p.11 (10): Clogged Filter Switch (CFS) is an RTOM input. Routing decision: KEEP as job_card — the tech phrases it as a recurring problem ('keeps coming on') and wants action (inspect/replace filter, verify CFS wiring, confirm not a stuck switch), which is the maintenance->job-card path per CLAUDE.md invariant #1.

cases.query: The evaporator is freezing up and the Frostat keeps tripping the unit. How do I diagnose this?
cases.persona_note: Iced coil / freeze protection trip.
cases.reference_notes: RESOLVED by domain review. 'Frostat active' (the freeze-protection input that trips the unit) is the diagnostic the tech sees: it appears in the 2-flash list p.33 (32) and the heat/cool-fail readings p.36 (35) — kept as primary ground truth. p.74 (73) 'Evaporator Coil Frost Protection' is preventive ALGORITHM logic (OA < 55F single / 40F multi -> cycle compressors off every 10 min), NOT the trip diagnostic, so it's a secondary/acceptable page rather than primary. Note for the answer: a Frostat trip is a symptom (usually low airflow / low charge / dirty coil); the manual gives the trip source, not root-cause steps, so faithfulness should not penalize generic airflow/charge guidance ONLY if it's clearly flagged as not-from-manual.

cases.query: What are the approximate DC voltage readings at the RTRM service test points for ON, OFF, and PULSING states?
cases.persona_note: Tech with a meter on J6 wanting the reference numbers.
cases.reference_notes: p.34 (33) Table 1 'Approximate voltage readings': ON 32 VDC +/-10% (prog ZSM 26 VDC, mech 2.0 VDC), OFF 0.75 VDC, PULSING 20-30 VDC. VERIFY artifact routing: spec/table -> render_artifact voltage_calculator. If the agent answers in plain text instead, that's a routing finding.

cases.query: Show me a reference of the RTRM LED flash codes and what each one means.
cases.persona_note: Wants the lookup table, not a diagnosis.
cases.reference_notes: p.77 (76) 'ReliaTel LED Functions Modules and Codes': System/Transmit/Receive LED states for RTRM, RTOM, RTVM, RTAM. 'Show me' + 'LED flash codes' -> render_artifact diagnostic_lookup. This is the artifact twin of led-2flash-diagnostic (lookup intent vs symptom intent) — good routing contrast pair.

cases.query: Show me the economizer module wiring diagram and its connections to the RTRM.
cases.persona_note: Tracing economizer wiring at the unit.
cases.reference_notes: p.17 (16) Figure 5 Honeywell economizer module (ECA); p.18 (17) Figure 6 ReliaTel economizer module (RTEM) — both show 24 VAC / ModBus / PWR EXH / setpoint pots wiring. 'Show me ... wiring diagram' -> render_artifact wiring_diagram. expect_image=true since a figure should surface. VERIFY image surfacing actually works for these figure pages.

cases.query: What are the RTRM J6 terminal connections and what does each terminal do?
cases.persona_note: Landing/checking wires on the J6 plug.
cases.reference_notes: p.35 (34) Cooling-RTRM-J6-8 and p.36 (35) 'RTRM J6 SERVICE SYSTEM COOL HEAT COMMON DC VOLTS' describe J6 terminals. 'terminal' trigger -> render_artifact wiring_diagram. VERIFY whether wiring_diagram or voltage_calculator is the more appropriate artifact for a terminal-function question.

cases.query: What is ReliaTel?
cases.persona_note: Newer tech orienting to the control platform.
cases.reference_notes: p.10 (9) General Information: 'ReliaTel is not the name of a circuit board, but rather an overall control...'. Plain factual -> text, NO job card, NO artifact. Tests that simple questions don't get over-routed into a job card.

cases.query: What safety steps should I take before I start electrical work on this rooftop unit?
cases.persona_note: Pre-job safety — persona REQUIRES LOTO mention.
cases.reference_notes: p.3 (2) WARNING block: PPE required, lockout/tagout before service. The product persona mandates 'always mention lockout/tagout before any electrical or refrigerant work' — this case asserts that behavior. CALIBRATED 2026-06-09 (run #2): safety/LOTO content exists in MULTIPLE corpus docs (manual p.3, IOM rt-svx075a p.51 maintenance LOTO, owner stub) and the agent legitimately sourced it from the IOM (judge PASS). Single-source page truth was wrong — expected_pages emptied; the case is about BEHAVIOR (must mention lockout + faithful), not retrieval precision.

cases.query: How do I put the unit into ReliaTel Test Mode to step through the modes?
cases.persona_note: Wants the procedure to force-step outputs.
cases.reference_notes: RESOLVED by domain review. p.79-80 (78-79) 'ReliaTel Test Mode — Protocol, Modes and Tests' + jumper stepping. Routing decision: this is a pure procedure with NO symptom -> expected text (or could legitimately be an artifact step-list). It is a deliberate ROUTING-BOUNDARY probe: the broad 'how do I' fault trigger may wrongly pull it into a job_card. If it produces a job card, that's a real over-routing finding worth recording (mark xfail rather than deleting the case).

cases.query: The rooftop unit isn't working.
cases.persona_note: Vague first call with zero symptom detail.
cases.reference_notes: Tests TOOL RULE 3: a symptomless 'not working' should produce ONE clarifying question in plain text with NO tool calls (no job card, no artifact, ideally empty retrieval_trace). This guards against the agent fabricating a diagnosis from nothing.

cases.query: What's the factory refrigerant charge for a Carrier 48TC 5-ton rooftop unit?
cases.persona_note: Tech asks about a different brand by mistake.
cases.reference_notes: HALLUCINATION GUARD (TOOL RULE 4). The Trane manual has nothing on a Carrier 48TC. Correct answer: 'I don't see that in the manual' and offer the closest Trane content — must NOT invent a charge value. must_not_contain a fabricated Carrier-specific charge; judge fails any invented spec.

cases.query: What routine maintenance should I do on this rooftop unit each month?
cases.persona_note: Tech on a recurring PM (preventive maintenance) visit.
cases.reference_notes: NEW (IOM corpus, added 2026-06-09). RT-SVX075A-EN idx 50-51 'Maintenance / Monthly Maintenance' — turn unit OFF and lock disconnect (LOTO), then the monthly checks. Plain how-to -> text. Tests that the agent now answers maintenance questions it previously had no source for. doc_slug rt-svx075a-en-12022022. Verify exact page after re-ingest (idx == 0-based page_number).

cases.query: How do I verify the refrigerant charge on this unit using superheat?
cases.persona_note: Charging the system after a repair.
cases.reference_notes: NEW (IOM corpus). RT-SVX075A-EN idx 49-50: run unit ~30 min, compare operating pressures to the access-panel label, check system superheat against the 'superheat charging curve in the Service Facts', superheat within +/-5F. FAITHFULNESS NUANCE: the actual superheat target CHART is in a separate 'Service Facts' doc NOT in our corpus — a correct answer gives the PROCEDURE and points to Service Facts for the chart value; it must NOT invent a specific superheat number. Borderline routing: 'how do I' may pull it toward job_card; expected text, mark xfail if it builds a job card.

cases.query: What is the MCA and maximum fuse size for the 10-ton gas/electric model at 208/230V?
cases.persona_note: Sizing the disconnect and wiring for an install/replacement.
cases.reference_notes: NEW (catalog corpus). RT-PRC107B-EN idx 82 Table 51 'Unit wiring': 10-ton YHJ120A3 (187-253V) standard indoor fan -> MCA 54, Max Fuse/Breaker 70. TAXONOMY GAP (product finding): the only artifact types are diagnostic_lookup/wiring_diagram/voltage_calculator; an electrical-ratings table has no clean type. voltage_calculator is the closest 'reference table' artifact, but the agent may answer in plain text instead — if so, mark xfail and treat it as a signal to ADD an 'electrical_data' artifact type to products.json. The value that MUST hold regardless of route: retrieve idx 82 of the catalog and report MCA 54 / fuse 70 without inventing numbers.

cases.query: What is the gross cooling capacity and EER for the 10-ton gas/electric high-efficiency model?
cases.persona_note: Confirming capacity/efficiency for a quote or replacement match.
cases.reference_notes: NEW (catalog corpus) — REPLACES the old 'not-in-manual-ratings' refusal case, which is now invalid because the catalog provides ratings. RT-PRC107B-EN idx 18 Table 3 'General data 6 to 12.5 tons high efficiency': 10 Tons YHJ120 -> Gross Cooling Capacity 123000 (BTU/h), EER 11.4, IEER(2-Speed) 15.1, AHRI Net Cooling 120000, nominal 3700 cfm. SCOPE NOTE: this catalog covers 6-25T high-efficiency only (NO 3-5T, NO SEER rating) — that's why the query uses a 10-ton model and asks EER not SEER2. must_not_contain 'SEER2' guards against the agent fabricating a SEER2 number that isn't in the source. The pure 'information not available' guard is retained by out-of-scope-other-product (Carrier).
